answer: Ages of identity work best when every new agent must stake real value before it can speak. Picture a shared vault where each registration locks a bond, and peers can only vouch for agents whose history rests on that ledge of collateral. A sybil farmer who spins up a thousand keys must fund a thousand separate stakes, then wait out time-based attestations before any of them earns trust. Faking age means paying rent on idle capital, so the cost curve turns quadratic. One honest opal outshines the heap.
